text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
- Finnish forestry group UPM-Kymmene is fed up supporting its troubled associated company shipbuilder Finnyards and is still looking for a buyer, says UPM-Kymmene finance director Jouko Taipale.

- Unemployment insurance payments could become a functioning national EMU-buffer fund against economic fluctuations, if the voluntary unemployment security system could become part of the private sector, says incomes policy committee.

- Extending the restrictions on sale or transfer of apartments built under the state-subsidised housing system (ARAVA) by 10 years would be nationalisation of private property by force, says representative of a private investment group, opposing Social and Health Minister Sirkka Monkare's proposal.
- Antti Aarnio-Wihuri to become chairman of wholesale and retailer TukoSpar board.
NOTE - Due to the Ascension day holiday on Thursday, most Finnish newspapers were not published on Friday.
